subject.title: Feature request: Shareable cron job templates

question: Should ClawHub support shareable scheduled-job templates as a first-class catalog/install surface, or keep cron examples within existing skills/plugins until OpenClaw defines scheduled-job install semantics?
rationale: The request is coherent, but it adds both a new catalog model and a recurring-action trust boundary, so automation should not choose the artifact family, consent flow, or runtime authority model.

options.title: Design an RFC first
options.body: Define schema, preview, install authority, moderation, and OpenClaw runtime semantics before implementation.

options.title: Use existing skills or plugins
options.body: Treat cron examples as normal skills or bundle plugins and avoid adding a new scheduled-template artifact type for now.

options.title: Defer to runtime contract
options.body: Keep the feature open but wait for OpenClaw runtime scheduled-job installation semantics before ClawHub catalog work.

recommendation.title: Design an RFC first
recommendation.body: Define schema, preview, install authority, moderation, and OpenClaw runtime semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen has the strongest current-history ownership across package schema, API docs, acceptable-use policy, RFC template, and product guardrails relevant to this decision.
